summary: pystr-codec ships a.pth dropper that fetches the Bun runtime and executes a 17MB obfuscated JS payload at Python startup
details: The package installs pystr_codec-setup.pth, which Python executes on every interpreter startup. The.pth runs embedded code that downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.2.18) from github.com/oven-sh to a temp path, chmods it executable, and invokes `bun run ci.js` against a 17MB obfuscated JavaScript file shipped inside the package. A /tmp/.bun_ran marker gates the drop to once per temp lifetime. ci.js is multi-layer obfuscated: an initial eval of a hex-decoded, Caesar-shifted string reconstructs an AES-128-GCM decryption helper using node:crypto and then decrypts further hex-encoded blobs at runtime, so the executed code is only materialized inside the Bun process. The package presents itself as 'Python string codec utilities' authored by 'pydev', but pystr_codec/__init__.py is empty and no codec functionality is shipped — the only functional artifacts are the.pth dropper and the obfuscated ci.js. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern deliberately moves execution outside the Python-visible sandbox, and the cover-story naming plus deep obfuscation of a 17MB payload are consistent with hostile intent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
